chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Jam sessions at the Nest with Bechet, Dunn and Bussey
summary: Albertson asks about sitting in; Wooding recalls musicians coming up after two in the morning to take choruses on four-beat numbers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We're getting -- yeah, I just want to stay on that one thought before we stray far from it. There was much more, in those days, of sitting in, you know of, you'd drop in to a club and you'd play with them, or somebody'd drop into your club and play with you. I would imagine that that inspired a lot of music. People getting together informally and just jamming together. Which is something we don't have any more,

No, that's what you miss. You miss that experience. Now when we were in the Nest, way back in the days of the Nest, Henry Bussey, Frank Forani, Johnny Dunn, Tommy Morris, these are fellows all used to come up. Bechet, Sidney Bechet, all of them used to come up and sit with band and play a time. See, when we were doing our arrangements, [we never], but we always had some numbers like "Georgia Brown", "Strutters' Ball", and things like that where we'd say, "Dear Old Southland", okay and things like that, where we'd play just some, four beat, we'd say, "Alright, go into four beats." And we'd play that, and these fellows would all take turns and take the chorus. And I think it was quite a lot of help to many of them. Because they was able to exchange ideas right on the floor and they used to line right up in front of the band, and it would just be myself and the guitar player and the drummer and the bass and the other guys were glad to -- like Garvin Bushell and the other Saxophone player and Bobby and them would be glad to get that -- go off.
And we'd sit down there and play for an hour sometimes. And this would always happen after around two o'clock, you see.
That of course, was also a great experience for the audience.

Oh, of course, it's what they wanted. Otherwise the man would have stopped them. Sometimes they could dance, and sometimes they could just sit and listen to it. If there was anything exceptionally going on, they would just listen to it.
